mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Y/Y GDPC1 growth accelerates by >1pp but SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM Manufacturing Index (proxied by INDPRO) falls below 50, indicating a contraction in manufacturing activity, it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy enters a slowdown or recession.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 50 but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate, defined as the UNRATE rising by >0.5pp in 3 months, signals a rapidly weakening labor market and impending recession, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises >0.5pp in 3mo but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in >40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, indicating a restrictive monetary policy, it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs weigh on economic activity and earnings.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (proxied by HOUST) decline by >10% year-over-year, it signals a weakening housing market and consumer spending, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Y/Y HOUST declines >10% but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in >40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by >200k jobs per month for 3 consecutive months, it signals an overheating labor market that will lead the Fed to aggressively raise rates, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS grows >200k/mo for 3mo but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in >40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, it signals that the Fed is behind the curve on inflation and will need to aggressively raise rates, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS < 2% but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When real consumer spending (RSAFS) declines by >5% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by >0.5pp over the same period, it signals a rapidly weakening consumer and impending recession, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Y/Y RSAFS declines >5% and UNRATE rises >0.5pp but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in >40% of instances.
